components.name: webhook-platform-coverage-report
components.description: P1-28: not a real module - it ships no code of its own. It exists only so jacoco-maven-plugin's report-aggregate goal has a project whose *dependencies* are the four real modules, which is how JaCoCo discovers their target/classes and target/jacoco*.exec at reactor build time (report-aggregate walks the current project's dependency list, not the reactor's modules list - a plain multi-module pom parent is not enough on its own). Threshold enforcement (jacoco:check) deliberately does NOT live here: the check goal, unlike report-aggregate, only ever reads a single `dataFile` against ITS OWN project's compiled classes - it has no equivalent of report-aggregate's dependency-walking, so binding it in a pom-packaging module with no classes of its own just silently skips ("missing execution data file:.../webhook-platform-coverage-report/target/jacoco.exec"), which was tried and confirmed dead-on-arrival during this task's own verification (see the Progress log in .claude/features/P1-28-coverage-tooling.md). Each of common/api/worker/cli therefore declares its own `check` execution against its own merged coverage instead - see the jacoco-merge execution in the root pom for how that per-module merged file gets built, and each module's own pom.xml for its threshold rules. Declared last in the root pom's modules list so the reactor builds it after common/api/worker/cli have already produced their classes and exec data (Maven also reorders by the dependency graph below regardless, so this is belt-and-braces).
